status: Owner-requested partial geography playtest; broader acceptance incomplete
scope: Earth-like local regions, geological landforms, ground surfaces and vegetation. Animals/humans/weather/sky behaviour excluded.
limitations: 100+FPS everywhere at Medium is not achieved: tall-savanna travel remains about 92FPS and travel frame-time tails exceed 10ms.
Offscreen fixed-site benchmarks are not universal whole-game guarantees; independent GPU timing samples unavailable.
True river distributary deltas, fjords, arches, complete barrier-island systems, eruptions and caves remain unimplemented.
Landforms remain a game approximation with visible texture repetition and stylized silhouettes.
The /landmark command searches bounded generated candidates and may not find every suitable example.

native_cases.findings: Inspected current wet-context entrance: complete shelter, bedding and cleared floor with surrounding forest retained. Physical entry/exit, lifecycle and current binary save/load are tested; long performance profiling intentionally omitted for this owner-requested handoff.

Inspected current cold-context entrance: fitted complete hide cover and accessible doorway on a slope. Dawn lighting is a mechanics-regression context. Physical entry/exit, lifecycle and current binary save/load are tested; no broad FPS claim.

Inspected final current waterfall: visible aeration, variable streaks and broken dithered edges; it reads as flowing water rather than the earlier grey rectangular face. Still a stylized prototype; no full volumetric spray. Actual fixed-camera frames show motion; native landmark visits dry ground. Corrected final package additionally survives normal post-landmark updates without stale animal chart projection errors.

Same final43/38 volcanic geometry in an earlier package: overhead shows the dropped floor and steep inner scarp. Close rim view remains plain. Numerical12-site/shared-edge checks and native landmark visit passed. Water rendering was subsequently refined; this package is explicitly historical.

Historical same-geometry reference: broad incised terraces and gullies with continuous rendered water. More varied than the baseline, but walls remain gamified and rhythmic and the water corridor is broad; not a complete Grand Canyon reconstruction.

Historical same-geometry reference: forested carbonate towers and intervening valleys, fractured steep faces. Ground forest floor is dark/subtle; some tiled rock remains. Grounding audit found 59059 roots, zero missing resident ground, maximum error 0.000041m.
Historical same-geometry reference: finite asymmetric isolated red outcrop with fractured weathering; broad silhouette is still stylized and some texture repetition remains.
